recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If valid SNOMED CT content regresses on tx.fhir.org, address the terminology server content/package or operations process rather than the FHIR core spec checkout.
issue_request: FHIR-19963 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core change request, raised against STU3 and applied for R5, reporting that tx.fhir.org failed to find valid SNOMED CT code 733104004; the resolution was auto-approved.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly tagged with FHIR-19963 was found in the FHIR source checkout. The closest current source/configuration evidence is tools/ig/ig.json:12, which has long configured the SNOMED CT International edition URI and was added by non-Jira-tagged commit 687135eb56e408b442bccf7b86a40ee5815c9bba before this issue.
additional_context: Current core source identifies SNOMED CT as an external code system and says base FHIR uses concepts from the International distribution. tools/tx/snomed/snomed.xml is a build cache for concepts referenced by the specification, not the full tx.fhir.org content store, and tracked core source contains no 733104004 entry. Live tx.fhir.org/r5 validation and lookup for http://snomed.info/sct code 733104004 now succeed, returning display "Buccal swab" and International edition version 20250201. Community searches found no direct FHIR-19963 Zulip or Confluence evidence changing that conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit. No FHIR core source was changed because the reported failure belongs to operational terminology-server content; adding an arbitrary valid SNOMED CT code to the checked-in source cache would not be a correct current-spec fix.
